sections.h2: Where is Draper, Utah, and why does the county line matter when you sell?
sections.html:
Draper sits on the Wasatch Front about 20 miles south of Salt Lake City, and the city spans two counties: Salt Lake County and Utah County. It covers roughly 30 square miles at an elevation of 4,751 feet, with Sandy to the north, South Jordan to the northwest, Riverton and Bluffdale to the west, and Lehi, Highland and Alpine to the south and southeast.

The city describes itself as sitting at the Point of the Mountain, the narrow gap between the south end of the Salt Lake Valley and the north end of Utah Valley. For a seller, the county line decides which assessor values the house, which treasurer sends the tax bill and which recorder files the deed. The school district changes too: the Salt Lake County side is served by Canyons School District and the Utah County side by Alpine School District.

Check your parcel number before you plan anything. Two neighbors a few blocks apart can deal with different county offices, different tax calendars and different school boundaries.

sections.h2: What is the history of Draper in brief?
sections.html:
Draper began as a cattle and farming settlement in the fall of 1849, when Ebenezer Brown grazed cattle near South Willow Creek. His wife's brother, William Draper Jr., joined the family in 1850, and about twenty families lived in the area by the end of 1852.

The first post office opened in 1854 under the name Draperville. That same year Ebenezer Brown gave land near 12650 South 900 East for a fort, though the walls were never finished. By the 1940s the town was known as the Egg Basket of Utah, and Draper became a city in 1978.

The growth since then is striking. The 2020 census counted 51,017 people in Draper, up from 7,257 in 1990. Many of the neighborhoods you see today were built in that window, so houses in the city range from old farm lots to subdivisions less than a generation old.

sections.h2: What does the Draper economy look like?
sections.html:
Draper is part of the Silicon Slopes tech corridor, and the city reports more than 1,000 businesses. Company headquarters or major offices named in public sources include 1-800 Contacts, Control4, HealthEquity, Pluralsight and Synchrony Bank, along with Dealertrack, Trader Joe's and Tesla in the city's own list. Utah's first IKEA opened in Draper in 2007.

The Utah State Prison operated in Draper from 1951 to 2022, and it ranked in the top employer size band (1,000 to 1,999 workers) in a fiscal 2018 snapshot.

Getting around is straightforward by Utah standards. Interstate 15 runs through the area, UTA's TRAX Blue Line stops at Draper Town Center and Kimballs Lane, and a FrontRunner commuter rail station is also in the city. Salt Lake International Airport and Provo Municipal Airport are each about 30 minutes away by car, according to the city.

The owner-occupied rate of 68.6% is lower than in Herriman, Farmington or Eagle Mountain, so roughly 31% of occupied Draper homes are rented. If you are selling a rental, the tenant situation matters as much as the building.

sections.h2: Does wildfire risk affect a Draper house sale?
sections.html:
It can, especially for homes along the foothills. In December 2025 the Draper City Council adopted Ordinance 1695, which created a Wildland Urban Interface Area in the city code. The public notice does not map the boundaries or list the rules, so ask the city for the full ordinance if your lot backs onto open hillside.

A separate state program adds another layer. Utah House Bill 48 of 2025 led the state forestry division to publish a wildfire risk map that scores each building from 1 to 8. A building that scores 7 or higher and sits within 250 meters of at least two other buildings falls inside the high-risk boundary, and owners of those buildings may owe the state an annual fee once the program starts, which the state expected later in 2026.

  • Look up the address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov before you list or accept an offer.
  • Keep a printout of the score for the buyer or title company.
  • Ask the Draper City planning office whether your lot falls inside the new city interface area.

sections.h2: What are Draper's rules for short-term rentals and accessory units?
sections.html:
Draper requires two approvals to run a short-term rental: a business license and a short-term rental permit. A stay counts as short term when it is under 30 consecutive days, the minimum stay is two nights, and the permit has to be renewed every year. Each day of unpermitted operation is a separate violation.

Accessory dwelling units have their own limits.

  • A detached ADU needs a residential lot of at least 12,000 square feet.
  • An internal ADU generally needs a residential lot over 6,000 square feet on a qualifying street, and the city has mapped areas where internal units are banned.
  • The owner must live in the main dwelling for both types.
  • Rentals of an ADU must run at least 30 consecutive days, and each needs one extra on-site parking space.

A basement apartment that was built without a permit is a common snag. The city's ADU page says owners who did not apply by February 1, 2022 face immediate enforcement, so a buyer who needs financing may hesitate over one. Draper's planning office takes questions at (801) 576-6399.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled on a Draper home?
sections.html:
Your county's calendar controls the bill, and Utah gives primary residences a 45% exemption so that only 55% of market value is taxed. Rental homes can qualify as primary residences under the state's rules, while vacation homes cannot.

For a Salt Lake County parcel, the county lists these dates:

  • July 22: valuation notices are mailed.
  • August 1 to September 15: the Board of Equalization takes valuation appeals.
  • November 1: official tax notices go out.
  • November 30: last day to pay without penalty.
  • December 1: unpaid taxes become delinquent, with a penalty of the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel.

A Utah County parcel follows the same November 30 due date, with notices mailed around the third week of October. Delinquent parcels in Utah County face a penalty of $10 or 1%, whichever is greater, on December 1. If your house is on the market when the notice arrives, tell the title officer so the current-year bill is handled correctly at closing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Draper?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Draper follows the same steps as any Utah sale, minus the lender. You give us the address and a few details, we review the house, and if the offer works you pick the closing date with a title company.

  1. Tell us about the house, including any tenants, liens or repairs.
  2. We look at the property and the recent sales around it.
  3. You decide whether to accept the offer or walk away.
  4. A title company runs the title search and prepares the closing paperwork.
  5. The deed is recorded with the county recorder where the parcel sits.

Recording is cheap. Salt Lake County charges a flat $40 recording fee, and Utah County lists the same $40 standard fee per document. Salt Lake County asks for a notary acknowledgment, the grantee's address and the tax serial number on the deed.

sections.h2: What do Draper sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
A short list of issues tends to slow a Draper sale.

  • A hillside lot with a high state wildfire score.
  • An older basement unit with no ADU permit.
  • A short-term rental permit that lapsed after its annual renewal.
  • A tenant in place on a rental, since roughly 31% of occupied homes are not owner-occupied.
  • Confusion over whether the parcel is billed by Salt Lake County or Utah County.

Any of these can be solved, but each adds steps to a traditional listing. A direct sale lets you sell the house as it stands and deal with the paperwork at the title company.

faqs.q: Is Draper in Salt Lake County or Utah County?
faqs.a: Both. Draper lies in Salt Lake County and Utah County, so the county for your tax bill and deed depends on the parcel. Look up the parcel number on your tax notice to see which county applies.

faqs.q: When are Draper property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30, whichever county bills you. Salt Lake County lists November 30 as the last day to pay without penalty, and Utah County does the same. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday it moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Draper house on a short-term basis?
faqs.a: Yes. Draper requires both a business license and a short-term rental permit, and the permit must be renewed each year. Operating without both is a violation, and each day counts separately.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Draper house that has an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell it, but expect questions. Draper requires an ADU permit before an accessory unit is rented, and the owner must live in the main dwelling. A cash buyer can take the house as it is, while a bank-financed buyer may ask you to resolve the permit first.

faqs.q: How do I check wildfire risk for a Draper address?
faqs.a: Search the address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov. The portal shows a structure exposure score from 1 to 8, and the state treats buildings scoring 7 or higher near other buildings as high risk.
